title: Add timeout to HTTP requests in download_file
description: `requests.get(url, allow_redirects=True)` at `main.py:111` has no timeout. A slow or hung server will block the script indefinitely.\n\nFix: add `timeout=30` (or configurable via config.ini) to the `requests.get()` call.

title: Add validation for missing [Lists] section in config.ini
description:
`main.py:30`: `config['Lists']` raises `KeyError` if the `[Lists]` section is absent from `config.ini`. This produces an unhelpful traceback.

Fix: check `if 'Lists' not in config` after reading the config and raise a clear error: `raise ValueError('config.ini is missing the [Lists] section')`.

title: Add HTTP status check after download in download_file
description: `download_file()` at `main.py:111` does not check the HTTP status code. A 404 or 500 response silently writes error HTML/JSON to the temp file, which then gets parsed as a domain list and could inject garbage entries into Cloudflare Gateway.\n\nFix: call `r.raise_for_status()` after the request, before writing the file.

title: Replace print() with logger in cloudflare.py
description:
`cloudflare.py:51`: `print('Created list ' + name)` is mixed with structured `logger` calls throughout the module. This inconsistency means the message bypasses log level filtering and formatting.

Fix: replace with `logger.info(f'Created list {name}')`.

title: Use .get('result') to safely access API response in cloudflare.py
description:
`cloudflare.py:31` and `cloudflare.py:77`: `r.json()['result'] or []` handles `None` but raises `KeyError` if the Cloudflare API returns an unexpected error body that lacks the `'result'` key entirely.

Fix: use `r.json().get('result') or []` in both locations.

title: Fix overly broad hosts file detection in convert_to_domain_list
description:
`main.py:124-127`: The hosts file check scans the entire file content string (`if ip in data`) rather than individual lines. An IP address appearing in a comment (e.g., `# source: 127.0.0.1`) would falsely flag a plain domain list as a hosts file, causing every domain to be incorrectly parsed as a hosts entry.

Fix: check per-line — only consider a line as a hosts entry if it starts with a known IP prefix after stripping comments.

title: Improve resilience of new-slot cleanup phase
description:
`main.py:48-52`: The new slot is cleaned up before new lists are created. If `delete_list()` raises partway through cleanup, the script exits leaving the slot in an inconsistent state. On the next run, the cleanup will be retried, but there's no logging or indication of partial cleanup state.

Fix: wrap the cleanup loop in a try/except, log warnings on individual delete failures, and continue rather than crashing — orphaned lists in the new slot are non-critical since they'll be cleaned up on the next run.

title: Fix unclosed file handles in main.py
description:
Two places open files without context managers, leaking handles and lacking error handling.

- `main.py:18` in `loadWhitelist()`: `open('whitelist.txt', 'r').read().split('
')` — no context manager, crashes in `__init__` before logging is configured if file is missing
- `main.py:114` in `download_file()`: `open(path, 'wb').write(r.content)` — no context manager

Fix: wrap both in `with open(...) as f:` and add appropriate error handling. Also use `.splitlines()` instead of `.split('
')` to handle Windows line endings.
close_reason: Fixed both unclosed file handles: loadWhitelist now uses context manager with FileNotFoundError handling and splitlines(); download_file now uses context manager for writing

title: Remove redundant os.environ.get fallback in cloudflare.py
description:
`cloudflare.py:12`: `os.getenv(x) or os.environ.get(x)` — `os.getenv` is simply an alias for `os.environ.get`, so the `or` fallback is always redundant and never used.

Fix: simplify to `CF_API_TOKEN = os.getenv('CF_API_TOKEN')` and `CF_IDENTIFIER = os.getenv('CF_IDENTIFIER')`.

title: Replace pandas with lightweight deduplication
description:
`main.py:37`: `pandas` is imported only for `pd.unique(pd.array(all_domains))`. This is a heavy dependency (~30MB) for a single deduplication operation.

Fix: replace with `unique_domains = list(dict.fromkeys(all_domains))` which preserves insertion order and has no extra dependencies. Remove the `import pandas as pd` line and pandas from requirements.

title: Move logging.basicConfig before App instantiation
description: `logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)` is called inside `App.run()` at `main.py:21`, but `self.logger` is already used in `__init__` via `loadWhitelist()`. Log messages emitted during init are silently dropped.\n\nFix: move `logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)` to the module level (before `App()` is instantiated in `__main__`).
close_reason: Moved logging.basicConfig to __main__ block before App() instantiation so init-time log messages are not dropped

title: Fix IndexError crash in hosts file parsing
description: `main.py:139`: `line.split()[1]` crashes with `IndexError` if a hosts file line contains only one token (e.g., just an IP address with no hostname, or a line with trailing whitespace only).\n\nFix: split into a variable first and guard: `parts = line.split(); if len(parts) < 2: continue; domain = parts[1].rstrip()`
close_reason: Split hosts file line into parts variable first, skip lines with fewer than 2 tokens to prevent IndexError

title: Fix blue/green swap logic to use stable policy ordering
description:
`main.py:41`: The active/standby slot detection uses `cf_policies[0]['name'].startswith(...)`, assuming the Cloudflare API returns policies in a consistent order. If ordering changes, the script could delete the wrong (active) policy.

Fix: find the active policy by explicitly searching both prefixes rather than relying on list position, e.g. check whether any policy name contains `_A` or `_B` to determine which slot is currently live.
close_reason: Replaced cf_policies[0] index check with any() scan across all returned policies to determine active slot independent of API ordering

title: Use or remove is_valid_hostname in domain processing
description:
`main.py:94`: `is_valid_hostname()` is defined but never called. Domains are added to the list without validation, so malformed hostnames can be sent to the Cloudflare API and cause errors.

Fix: call `is_valid_hostname(domain)` in `convert_to_domain_list()` before appending, and skip (with a debug log) any domains that fail validation. If the method is intentionally unused, remove it.
